content:
Purpose: To develop and evaluate a locally deployed multi-agent AI system for structuring radiology reports and providing quality assurance.

Materials and Methods: In this retrospective study, 638 radiology reports from CT examinations of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis—dictated by 15 board-certified radiologists in 2023 and 2024—were analyzed. A multi-agent AI pipeline was developed to perform report structuring and quality assurance (QA). The system organized reports into standardized anatomical sections at the sentence level using a combination of regular expression rules and locally hosted large language models. It also identified mismatches between the Findings and Impression sections or within sections, gender-anatomy inconsistencies, and undocumented communication of critical findings. Two board-certified radiologists independently reviewed a subset of 45 reports.

Results: The multi-agent system structured the Findings sections of all reports (22,270 sentences) into a predefined anatomical format while preserving the original content. The system flagged 90 reports (14.1%), most commonly for section mismatches (80 reports, 12.5%). In the radiologist evaluation, both reviewers agreed that 31 reports (69%) were correctly restructured, 2 reports (4%) were incorrectly restructured, and disagreed on 12 reports (27%). Both reviewers agreed that no clinically important information was omitted and no fabricated content was introduced. Overall QA performance was rated as "excellent" or "good" in 84% of evaluated reports, with the remainder rated as "fair."

Conclusion: A locally deployed multi-agent AI system effectively integrated radiology report structuring and quality assurance into a unified workflow. The system demonstrated favorable performance in radiologist evaluation and may support standardization and quality assurance in radiology practice.
